watchlist.thesis: Post-earnings continuation remains strong: the stock gained 21.6% over the last 11 sessions and traded 2.6× its prior-10-session average volume on Nov 17; record backlog growth and free-cash-flow growth support the move, while lower reported revenue and project-execution risk argue against chasing gaps.

Post-results momentum accelerated 3.5% on Nov 17 with 3.2× its prior-10-session volume and a 13.8% 11-session gain; higher margins, adjusted EPS growth and stronger free cash flow support the move, but flat-to-down organic-sales guidance and leverage temper conviction.

A steady 8.7% 11-session advance and a strong StockLens technical reading align with Q4 adjusted EPS growth of 27%, revenue growth of 5.4% and free-cash-flow growth of 42%; healthcare weakness and only average recent volume favor patient entries.

A strong StockLens technical reading and a Nov 17 close 0.09% above the open on 1.9M shares support a defensive industrials setup in a weak tape; without a fresh company catalyst, favor pullbacks and require renewed relative-strength confirmation.

sector_notes: U.S. breadth was sharply negative on Nov 17: 2,904 stocks priced at least $5 with at least 500K shares traded showed 663 advancing versus 2,195 declining on an open-to-close basis; the S&P 500 fell 1.03% and the VIX rose to 25.46. Energy and industrials were the relative leaders on the down day, while financials were the weakest sector and all 11 S&P sectors finished lower, favoring selective post-earnings continuation over broad momentum exposure. Technology and semiconductors remain vulnerable after the latest AI-led selloff, so avoid concentrated high-beta exposure.
